stories.title: SHEIN Pull & Chew Montessori Teething Toy Recall — 644 Units, Choking Hazard
stories.angle: CPSC recall of SHEIN Pull & Chew Montessori teething toys — about 644 units. Silicone strings are too long and thin, can reach the back of a baby's throat, and pose a deadly choking hazard. Stop use immediately; cut strings; email productrecall@shein.com with photo for refund.

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: ⚠️ SHEIN Pull & Chew teething toys recalled — about 644 units. Silicone strings are a choking hazard. Stop use now. Cut strings and email productrecall@shein.com with photo for refund. No injuries yet. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: The recalled SHEIN toys are silicone — green, pink, yellow, or blue. Sold on SHEIN.com Dec 2025–Apr 2026 for about $10. Cut the strings and email productrecall@shein.com with a photo for a full refund. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

stories.title: VFC COVID Vaccines for 2026-27 Available — But Shipment Delays Hit Low-Income Kids
stories.angle: COVID vaccines have been added to the federal Vaccines for Children (VFC) program for 2026-27, but the CDC has not provided a shipment timeline. About half of U.S. children qualify for free VFC vaccines (Medicaid, uninsured, underinsured, American Indian/Alaska Native). The delay means low-income kids may get their shots weeks or months after privately insured children.

stories.title: Rock Ledge Ranch Harvest Festival — Oct 3, Tickets $4–$8
stories.angle: Rock Ledge Ranch Historic Site hosts its annual Harvest Festival on Saturday, October 3, 2026, 10am–4pm. Wagon rides, pumpkins ($5 each), old-time music, cider-making demos, candy scramble, food trucks, and tours of historic homes. Tickets $4–$8; kids two and under free.

stories.title: COS 2026 Park System Master Plan — Public Comment Closed, What's Next for Families
stories.angle: Colorado Springs' 2026 Park System Master Plan public comment period closed September 22. The plan guides parks, trails, open spaces, and community centers for years ahead. Also: the Mary Starsmore Discovery Plaza — opened June 2026 at North Cheyenne Cañon Park — is the newest example of the city's investment in family-friendly park infrastructure.
